scope: Same-host original Orca L0 / native DG2 / original Orca L0; bounded context diagnostic, no code or production changes.

historical_context.caveat: The historical run used one long warmup; this run uses three. They are separate backend brackets, not an isolated causal comparison of runtime revisions.

validation.native_module_audit: No Intel UMD, Level Zero, compiler, GMM, SYCL or UR loaded in the native process.

caveats: Latest native revision uses explicit-dependency recording, zero-SLM preference and calibrated dependency flushes. Same A770, 5771 fixed expert slots, balanced spec-min-p=0.5, requested VRAM reserve 1536 MiB; production files unchanged.
Short is the prior 28-token natural76 anchor; long prompts reuse measured Code2K/Long8K inputs, with 64-token cap.
Case order is Short28, Code2K, Long8K in every process. Cache adaptation remains enabled; no prefix reuse.
Decode excludes initialization/loading/preparation/prefill; prompt, TTFT and request time reported separately.
Ten short warmups, three long warmups per case; five short and three long retained requests. This is a bounded diagnostic, not broad PPL.
Host/protocol observations, not GPU timestamps. Unlocked clocks, populated OS caches, no concurrent GPU experiment.

All graphs use the latest validated explicit ordering, zero-SLM and dependency-flush policies. This is original Orca L0 through Intel UMD versus the native replacement; it is not original SYCL versus Orca.
Long-prompt requests can continue adapting the expert cache after the three discarded warmups; retained trends are reported, not silently treated as a converged plateau.
Prompt contents and MTP acceptance differ between cases. Per-case backend comparisons match all outputs/drafts, but cross-case gap changes alone do not isolate context length.
Official NEO source differences identify candidate optimizations, not a measurement of their individual contributions or a trace of the installed proprietary driver.
